questions.question: The Doppler effect is the change in:
options: The frequency of sound detected by a listener because source and listener move relative to the medium
The speed of sound as a source accelerates
The loudness of a sound as it comes closer
The frequency at which the source itself vibrates

questions.question: Ahead of a moving siren, the wavefronts are:
options: Stretched apart, giving a longer wavelength
Bunched together, giving a shorter wavelength and higher detected frequency

questions.question: As a source moves through air, the speed of the sound waves it emits:
options: Stays fixed — it is a property of the medium

questions.question: An approaching ambulance sounds both louder and higher-pitched. The Doppler effect explains:
options: The pitch change only — loudness is about amplitude and distance

questions.question: In the Doppler equation, a source moving TOWARD a stationary listener requires:
options: Subtracting vs in the denominator, making the detected frequency higher

questions.question: A 900 Hz siren approaches a stationary listener at 30 m·s⁻¹ (v = 340 m·s⁻¹). The detected frequency is:
Once the same siren has passed and recedes at 30 m·s⁻¹, the detected frequency becomes:
The safest way to choose the plus or minus signs is to:
options: Always add in the numerator and subtract in the denominator
Memorise one sign pattern for all cases
Use whichever signs give a rounder number
Decide first whether the frequency should rise or fall, then pick signs to match

questions.question: A car drives at 20 m·s⁻¹ toward a stationary 500 Hz siren (v = 340 m·s⁻¹). The driver hears:
A stationary listener hears an 800 Hz hooter as 850 Hz. The train must be:
options: Approaching, because the detected frequency is higher than the source frequency
Stationary, with the wind carrying the sound

questions.question: Solving 850 = (340 ÷ (340 − vs)) × 800 gives a source speed of:
Doppler ultrasound measures blood flow speed by:
options: Timing how long the sound takes to cross the artery
Measuring how much sound the blood absorbs
Heating the blood slightly and tracking the warmth
Reading the frequency shift of ultrasound reflected off moving blood cells

subtopics.title: Red Shifts and the Expanding Universe

questions.question: A red shift in a galaxy's light means its spectral lines appear at:
options: Higher frequencies than in the laboratory
Lower frequencies than in the laboratory — the galaxy is receding
The same frequencies as in the laboratory

questions.question: Astronomers recognise that a distant galaxy's light is shifted by comparing:
options: Its colour with photographs from previous years
The pattern of an element's spectral lines with the same element's lines measured on Earth
The galaxy's size in the telescope

questions.question: The red shifts of distant galaxies provide evidence that:
options: The universe is expanding — galaxies are receding in every direction
The Earth is at the centre of the universe
Light slows down over large distances

questions.question: In the expanding universe, an observer in ANY galaxy would see:
options: Half the sky red-shifted and half blue-shifted
The same pattern — other galaxies receding in every direction, like raisins in rising dough

subtopics.title: The Siren That Lies to You

questions.question: To the paramedic riding inside the ambulance, the siren's pitch:
options: Rises as the vehicle speeds up
Stays constant — there is no relative motion between them and the siren
Falls as the vehicle passes buildings

questions.question: The pitch you hear drops the moment the ambulance passes because:
options: The driver switches the siren tone
Each crest is now launched from farther away, stretching the spacing between crests

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches the property of sound to what it measures?
options: Pitch — frequency; loudness — amplitude and distance

questions.question: In the analogy, the taxi rank's fixed ten-minute schedule stands for:
Walking toward the rank, you meet taxis more often. The sound equivalent is:
options: A source moving away from you
A listener moving toward the source, detecting a higher frequency

questions.question: The rolling taxi rank — dispatching on schedule while moving toward you — shows that a moving source:
options: Shrinks the gaps between successive taxis on the road ahead of it

questions.question: The reliable rule for the equation's signs is that motion of source and listener TOWARD each other must:

subtopics.title: From the Maternity Ward to the Whole Sky

questions.question: A clinic hears a foetal heartbeat by:
options: Amplifying the sound the heart makes directly
Passing a mild current through the skin
Translating the rhythmic Doppler shifts of ultrasound reflected off the moving heart wall

questions.question: Blood speeding up through a narrowed artery shows up in Doppler ultrasound as:
options: A larger frequency shift in the reflected sound

questions.question: "Slid red means moving away" summarises the finding that:
options: Red stars are always closer than blue stars
A receding light source's spectral fingerprint shifts toward lower frequencies
Red light travels slower than blue light

questions.question: The raisins-in-rising-dough picture teaches that the expansion of the universe:
options: Looks the same from every galaxy — no galaxy is the centre
Happens only near the edge of space
Pushes all galaxies toward one point
